svg.font-family: Georgia, 'Iowan Old Style', 'Times New Roman', serif
svg.title: game1 — the two-plate system
svg.desc: Reference sheet. One drawing, separated into an ink plate and a wash plate. The ink plate printed alone is the black-and-white edition; the identical ink plate over the wash plate is the colour edition.

g.text: One drawing, two plates. Black-and-white is not a reduced colour edition; colour is an added wash edition.
A · THE SAME DRAWING, THREE WAYS
Ale barrel · drink · the middle panel is why colour may never carry a rule. The body wash is the 55% under-ink tint; only the cast shadow, which carries no linework, prints at full strength.
B · THE ARCANE EXCEPTION — MAGIC IS A PRINTING ERROR
On arcane subjects only, the violet prints 1mm out of register and
bleeds past the black line — as though the press could never get
magic to sit still on the page.
No glow. No sparkle. No particles. There are two mana veins on the
whole board, and this is what makes that scarcity visible across a
table before anyone has read a number.
In black-and-white there is no slip, because there is no wash — and nothing is lost.
C · THE ELEVEN COMMODITY CATEGORIES — WASH LEFT, INK PLATE RIGHT
D · THE WHOLE PALETTE — FIVE CHROMATIC INKS, ONE BLACK, ONE PAPER
